content.value_statement: Teams need consistent SAST coverage across repositories and CI systems. This skill guides tool selection, pipeline setup, rule tuning, and result triage.
actual_capabilities: Explains setup choices for Semgrep, SonarQube, and CodeQL.
Shows CI/CD integration patterns for GitHub Actions and pre-commit hooks.
Provides example commands for baseline scans and compliance-focused scans.
Describes false positive tuning, suppressions, and rule optimization.
Compares common SAST tools by use case, language support, cost, and integration.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not include runnable helper scripts in this package.
It cannot decide organizational risk tolerance or compliance policy by itself.
It does not replace dynamic testing, manual review, or penetration testing.
Referenced asset and reference files are named in SKILL.md but are not included here.

use_cases.title: Launch SAST for a New Service
use_cases.description: Select suitable scanners, define an initial baseline, and add CI checks before release.

use_cases.title: Tune Noisy Security Scans
use_cases.description: Review false positives, document suppressions, and adjust rules so developers receive useful findings.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Plan recurring scans, produce SARIF or report outputs, and prioritize remediation for audit workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starter SAST Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a SAST tool for a repository using [languages]. My CI system is [CI system], and my main goal is [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Add SAST to CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a SAST CI workflow for [repository type]. Include scanner choice, trigger points, failure thresholds, and artifact handling.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce False Positives
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SAST finding summary and propose a tuning plan. Separate real risks, likely false positives, suppressions, and developer guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Tool Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SAST operating model for [organization]. Include Semgrep, SonarQube, CodeQL, quality gates, ownership, metrics, and rollout phases.

output_examples.input: We need SAST for a Python API in GitHub Actions.
output_examples.output: Recommended plan: start with Semgrep for fast security checks, add CodeQL for deeper analysis, and fail builds only on high confidence critical issues during the first baseline period.

output_examples.input: Our scan has many false positives in generated files.
output_examples.output: Expected output: an exclusion plan for generated paths, a suppression review checklist, and guidance for documenting accepted findings.

output_examples.input: Compare Semgrep, SonarQube, and CodeQL for our program.
output_examples.output: Expected output: a concise tool matrix with recommended roles, integration points, cost notes, and rollout priorities.

best_practices: Start in report-only mode, then enforce gates after the baseline is understood.
Pin scanner versions and container images before using commands in production pipelines.
Review suppressions regularly and keep evidence for accepted risks.
anti_patterns: Blocking all findings on the first scan without triage or baseline planning.
Uploading sensitive private code to third-party scanning services without approval.
Treating SAST results as complete proof that an application is secure.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill discuss?
faq.answer: It discusses Semgrep, SonarQube, and CodeQL for static application security testing.

faq.question: Can it generate final compliance policy?
faq.answer: No. It can structure scanner configuration and evidence workflows, but policy owners must approve requirements and risk thresholds.

faq.question: Does it run scans automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance and example commands that users can adapt and run with approval.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, if users choose approved tools and avoid sending sensitive code or logs to unauthorized services.

faq.question: Does it cover false positives?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for tuning rules, documenting suppressions, and reviewing noisy findings.

faq.question: Can it replace penetration testing?
faq.answer: No. SAST is one layer of security testing and should be combined with other review and testing methods.
